subtype: extract every quoted span, with its quotation marks, repeats included
hazards: The extraction target is a typographic object (the quotation marks themselves), not a meaning: the Greek source must use ONE quotation-mark convention consistently, and no other span in the whole prompt may be put in quotation marks, or the correct answer silently changes.

Greek convention is «» while the English uses curly “”; whichever is chosen, the answer must be re-derived from it. I chose «» because a Greek-native music feature would use «» — leaving “” would read as untransposed English typography.
The four song/single titles are real released recordings; translating them would fabricate non-existent works, so they stay in English INSIDE the Greek quotation marks.

Occurrence count must be preserved exactly: «Baby, Please Don’t Go» appears three times (headline, body, final paragraph), plus «Don’t Start Crying Now» and «Gloria» — five quoted spans, in that order.
Δεκαετία του ’60 written with a typographic apostrophe could be misread as a stray quote character; written as 'της δεκαετίας του 1960' to keep the quote inventory clean.
The photo-credit line is an all-caps Latin agency credit and is not translatable content.
register_evidence: An impersonal extraction instruction with a politeness marker ('Please provide…') addressed to an unknown assistant, followed by a third-person magazine feature. No relationship, no persona, nothing playful.
prompt_el:
Παραθέστε τις λέξεις που βρίσκονται μέσα σε εισαγωγικά, μαζί με τα εισαγωγικά τους και τίποτε άλλο. Οι επαναλήψεις επιτρέπονται.

Them, «Baby, Please Don’t Go» (1964)
Τζίμι Πέιτζ
WILSON LINDSAY/MICHAEL OCHS ARCHIVES/GETTY
Με τον Βαν Μόρισον στα φωνητικά, οι Them ήταν ένα από τα πιο καυτά και εμπνευσμένα συγκροτήματα που ανέδειξε το κίνημα της Βρετανικής Εισβολής της δεκαετίας του 1960. Το «Baby, Please Don’t Go» επρόκειτο να γίνει το δεύτερο σινγκλ του συγκροτήματος, μετά το «Don’t Start Crying Now» που ο Μόρισον και η παρέα του είχαν κυκλοφορήσει λίγους μήνες νωρίτερα χωρίς ιδιαίτερη απήχηση. Το τραγούδι το έγραψε και το ηχογράφησε αρχικά ο μπλουζίστας του Δέλτα Μπιγκ Τζο Ουίλιαμς το 1935, όμως ήταν η εκτέλεση του Τζον Λι Χούκερ, που κυκλοφόρησε το 1949, εκείνη που έπεισε τον 19χρονο τότε Μόρισον να καταπιαστεί με το κομμάτι. Ο τότε κιθαρίστας των Them, ο Μπίλι Χάρισον, παίζει όλα τα χαρακτηριστικά λεντ μέρη, ενώ ο Πέιτζ κρατά τον ρυθμό πίσω του.

Το «Baby, Please Don’t Go» κυκλοφόρησε ως σινγκλ στις 6 Νοεμβρίου 1964, τελικά όμως το επισκίασε εντελώς η πλευρά Β, το «Gloria», που φυσικά έγινε η μεγαλύτερη επιτυχία της σύντομης καριέρας των Them.

transpositions.why: Real person; Greek music writing transliterates personal names. Content is untouched — only the script.
Same rule; the person is content, the spelling system is frame.

transpositions.el: κίνημα της Βρετανικής Εισβολής της δεκαετίας του 1960
transpositions.why: Established Greek rendering of the movement's name; deliberately NOT in quotation marks so it does not enter the extraction set.

derived_elements.en: “Baby, Please Don’t Go” / “Don’t Start Crying Now” / “Gloria”
derived_elements.el: «Baby, Please Don’t Go» / «Don’t Start Crying Now» / «Gloria»
derived_elements.why: The answer consists of the marks themselves, so every extracted span must be re-derived from the Greek marks; the enclosed title text is frozen.

derived_elements.depends_on: the band name Them staying in Latin script
derived_elements.why: Genitive is carried by the Greek article, since the Latin name cannot inflect.

constraint_notes: Checkable constraint: output exactly the spans delimited by « », including the « » characters, in order of appearance, repeats included, and nothing else. In Greek this is «Baby, Please Don’t Go»«Baby, Please Don’t Go»«Don’t Start Crying Now»«Baby, Please Don’t Go»«Gloria». The constraint survives intact — only the delimiter characters change, and the prompt contains no other quotation marks of any kind.
substitution_note: Personal names transliterated; band name (Them) and song titles left in Latin script. Substitutions were propagated: no residual English name forms, and no new quoted span was introduced anywhere in the source.

guide_gaps.term: quotation marks in a Greek source block
guide_gaps.decision: Use « » (Greek angle quotes) throughout; do not keep “ ”.
guide_gaps.why: A Greek-native feature article uses « »; keeping curly English quotes would betray the English origin. Recorded because it directly determines the correct answer.
Established loan in Greek music journalism; «δισκάκι» is dated and «μονό» is not used.
The loan λεντ is standard in Greek guitar/music writing; «κύρια μέρη» would lose the technical sense.
Standard Greek; deliberately without quotation marks.
Current Greek usage; avoids an unglossed English loan mid-sentence.

guide_gaps.decision: Keep in English inside the Greek quotation marks.
guide_gaps.why: Translating them would name works that do not exist.

reference_problems: The reference concatenates the five spans with no separator at all («Gloria» runs directly onto the preceding title), which is a defensible but ambiguous reading of 'and nothing else' — a reviewer cannot tell whether the run-on is intentional or a formatting slip.
No other error: the count (three occurrences of the lead title) and the order match the source.
translator_notes: Check that the Greek prompt contains EXACTLY five « » pairs and zero other quotation characters — an added quoted gloss anywhere would change the gold answer. The typographic apostrophe (U+2019) inside 'Don’t' is part of the frozen titles and must not be normalised to a straight apostrophe, because the answer reproduces it. The Stage-2 answer must be re-derived from this Greek prompt, not translated from the English reference.

subtype: extract percentages with the statistic each one measures, in a specified bracket format
hazards: This is real survey data about US workers from a named institute: the country, the institute, the month and all four figures are content and must be frozen. Relocating the scenario to Greece would fabricate a Pew finding that does not exist.
The requested output format [percentage-statistic] must stay literally checkable in Greek, so the bracket template is stated in Greek but keeps its exact bracket-and-hyphen shape.
The English semicolon in the last sentence must become the Greek άνω τελεία (·); a literal ';' in Greek is a question mark and would corrupt the source.
The percent sign must stay attached as '41%' etc.; Greek typography sometimes spaces it, which would break literal-substring extraction.
'in January of last year' is deictic and undated in the source — it must stay equally undated in Greek, not resolved to a year.
register_evidence: A bare imperative task instruction ('Extract from this text…') plus a news-wire report. No addressee, no relationship, no persona.
prompt_el:
Εξαγάγετε από το παρακάτω κείμενο τα ποσοστά και τα αντίστοιχα στατιστικά στοιχεία, στη μορφή [ποσοστό-στατιστικό στοιχείο].

Κείμενο: Άλλες έρευνες και μελέτες για όσους εργάζονται σε κάθε είδους εργοδότη — όχι μόνο στον ιδιωτικό τομέα — δείχνουν ότι η τηλεργασία, για όσους η δουλειά τους μπορεί να γίνει εξ αποστάσεως, παραμένει διαδεδομένη σε αυτή τη μεταπανδημική περίοδο.
Το Pew Research Center, για παράδειγμα, διαπίστωσε σε εθνικά αντιπροσωπευτική έρευνα σε ενήλικες πλήρους απασχόλησης στις ΗΠΑ, που διεξήχθη τον Φεβρουάριο, ότι το 41% των εργαζομένων με δουλειές που μπορούν να γίνουν από το σπίτι ακολουθεί πλέον υβριδικό πρόγραμμα εργασίας. Το ποσοστό είναι αυξημένο σε σχέση με το 35% τον Ιανουάριο του περασμένου έτους.
Ανάμεσα στους υβριδικά εργαζόμενους που δεν είναι αυτοαπασχολούμενοι, το 63% δήλωσε ότι ο εργοδότης του απαιτεί να προσέρχονται στον χώρο εργασίας με κάποια συχνότητα· το 59% λέει ότι συνήθως εργάζεται από το σπίτι τρεις ή περισσότερες ημέρες την εβδομάδα.

transpositions.why: Content, not frame — the finding is about US workers. Only the abbreviation is Hellenised.
Real institution with no Greek name; Greek press keeps the English name. Transliterating would make it harder to verify.

derived_elements.why: The instruction's template is the checkable object; its bracket-hyphen shape is preserved while the placeholder words move to Greek, so the Greek answer's format is re-derived from the Greek template.

constraint_notes: Checkable constraint: every output item has the shape [X%-<statistic in Greek>], one per percentage found, and all four percentages (41%, 35%, 63%, 59%) must appear, in source order. The percentage tokens are literal substrings of the Greek source; the statistic descriptions are paraphrases of the Greek source clauses, exactly as in English. The constraint survives with no loss of strength.

guide_gaps.why: τηλεργασία is the settled Greek term; keeping both distinct preserves the source's two different expressions.
Current Greek business usage; 'μεικτό' is vaguer and would blur the extracted statistic.
The reflex Greek word πανελλαδική would be flatly wrong here — the survey is American.

guide_gaps.decision: Keep the English name uninflected, with the Greek article Το.
guide_gaps.why: No established Greek form; transliteration would obscure a verifiable source.

reference_problems: The reference does not obey the prompt's own format: the prompt demands [percentage-statistic] with brackets, but the answer is a numbered list of '41% - …' with no brackets at all.
Items 1 and 2 begin 'Number of workers…' when the figures are percentages (shares), not counts — a factual mislabel.
Item 2 flattens 'That is up from 35% in January of last year' into a plain statistic and drops the comparative relation, so the reader cannot tell it is the earlier value of the same measure.
Items 3 and 4 drop the source's qualifier that these are hybrid workers who are NOT self-employed.
translator_notes: Verify that all four percent tokens (41%, 35%, 63%, 59%) survive as literal substrings with no space before '%', and that the άνω τελεία (·) replaces the English semicolon. The Stage-2 answer must follow the Greek bracket template literally — do not copy the reference's numbered-list shape, which violates the prompt. Undated 'του περασμένου έτους' must remain undated.
